svg.text: PROPOSAL 12: the Japanese layout - one truck ramp from the existing signal, a public car park at dike height, the expressway moved south

North up, 50 m grid. Land, roads and today's viaduct are the built island's data; everything coloured is the proposal. Positions are from the round-6 measurements and are to be proven on a dry run before building.

g.text: WEST: public gate, right turn in / out
footbridge to the office and roof deck
ONE ramp, 5 % over ~125 m, with footway
EAST: main gate at the existing signal
coast road corner: one even curve (dashed)
expressway viaduct, deck 12 m over the water
expressway main line 16-20 m further south here (dashed)
NEW on-ramp: straight, one curve, straight
plain sea wall, fenced strip under the viaduct

svg.text: - ONE vehicle way down (the ramp); people also leave by the stairs, the footbridge or a boat. A second truck ramp would take the car park's place.
- Tan = new land: the west gap filled and the quay pushed out about 19 m along the whole shore, one straight line from the west gap to the east bank (x 270 to 720).
- East of the yard (x 610 to 720, under the viaduct) it is a plain vertical sea wall with a railing, not a working quay: fenced maintenance yard, a few parking bays, piers standing on land.
- The public car park is level with the dike road, so visitors never drive across the truck floor. Military base and harbour are not touched.
- The expressway piers are not drawn: they move with the main line. The new on-ramp joins about 55 m further west than today.
- The new on-ramp's curve touches the north edge of the ferris wheel park: the park can shift south a little to clear it.
